params.question: The principle of non-maleficence prohibits a clinician from performing any procedure that carries a risk of harm to the patient.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Non-maleficence does not prohibit all risk. The narration explained that many beneficial interventions carry inherent risk; what the principle requires is that risk be proportionate to expected benefit and not imposed carelessly. IPC Section 88 protects clinicians who act in good faith, even when some harm results.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Right. Non-maleficence does not require zero risk — many beneficial interventions carry inherent risk. What the principle requires is that risk be proportionate to expected benefit and that harm not be imposed carelessly. IPC Section 88 protects clinicians who act in good faith for a patient's benefit, even when harm results.

interactions.label: Dr. Anand treats a patient with a massive myocardial infarction, but no ECG find

params.question: Dr. Anand treats a patient with a massive myocardial infarction, but no ECG findings, drug doses, or clinical notes are recorded. When this case reaches a consumer court, how does the absence of documentation affect the proceedings?

answers.text: The court assumes the patient is exaggerating since no written evidence of substandard care exists

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The opposite is true — absent documentation disadvantages the clinician, not the patient. The legal standard is: if it wasn't written, it didn't happen.

answers.text: The court places the burden on Dr. Anand to prove that appropriate care was provided

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, NCDRC rulings confirm that absent documentation shifts the burden of proof to the clinician. Courts apply the standard: if it wasn't written, it didn't happen.

answers.text: Documentation is considered optional provided the patient ultimately survives the event

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Patient survival does not exempt a clinician from documentation obligations. The NMC Code of Conduct requires proper records for every clinical encounter regardless of outcome.

answers.text: The hospital's accreditation body must investigate independently before the court can proceed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: There is no mandatory pre-court investigation by accreditation bodies under the CPA 2019. The court directly applies the burden-of-proof standard to the available records.

overallFeedback.feedback: When documentation is absent, the burden of proof shifts to the clinician. The Consumer Protection Act 2019 and NCDRC rulings apply a clear standard: if it wasn't written, it didn't happen. Every note must carry a date, time, legible name, designation, full clinical findings, and an assessment with a plan.

Exactly. Multiple NCDRC rulings under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 confirm this standard — absent records shift the burden to the clinician. Documentation is a clinical act, not a bureaucratic chore.

interactions.label: A resident wonders whether adding metformin to insulin improves glycaemic contro

params.question: A resident wonders whether adding metformin to insulin improves glycaemic control in Type 2 diabetes patients compared to insulin alone. Using the PICO framework, which element represents the Comparator in this clinical question?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes the Population (P) — the patient group being studied, not what the intervention is compared against.
This describes the Outcome (O) — the measure used to evaluate effectiveness, not the comparator.

answers.text: Addition of metformin to the existing insulin regimen

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes the Intervention (I) — the treatment being assessed, not the standard it is compared to.
The Comparator (C) is the standard against which the intervention is measured. Here, insulin alone is what the new combination is being compared to.

overallFeedback.feedback: In the PICO framework, the Comparator (C) is the standard against which the intervention is measured — here, insulin therapy alone. Population is the patient group (Type 2 diabetes on insulin), Intervention is the new treatment (adding metformin), and Outcome is the measure of success (glycaemic control).

Correct. PICO turns a vague clinical uncertainty into a precise, searchable query — Population, Intervention, Comparator, and Outcome. Identifying each element correctly is essential for effective evidence searching.

params.question: A senior neurologist arrives for ward rounds with trembling hands, appears to be under the influence of alcohol, and prescribes valproate without checking the patient's pregnancy status. A junior resident observes this but stays silent. Which of the following best explains why this silence is problematic?

answers.text: The junior resident has not yet obtained independent practice registration and therefore cannot prescribe an alternative

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The reporting obligation concerns patient safety, not the reporter's prescribing authority. Any clinician who witnesses impairment creating risk has a duty to report, regardless of their own registration status.

answers.text: The NMC Act 2020 requires that impairment creating patient risk be reported, regardless of the colleague's seniority

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The NMC Act 2020 mandates reporting of impairment that creates patient risk. Seniority does not modify this obligation. As the narration warns, the most dangerous impaired colleague is one functional enough that peers rationalise inaction.

answers.text: Hospital bylaws mandate that only department heads can address substance-related concerns among consultants

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: No such restriction exists. The duty to report impairment applies to every clinician, not only department heads. Patient safety overrides hierarchical convenience.

answers.text: Reporting is recommended only after the impaired physician has been formally warned at least twice

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: There is no graduated warning threshold for reporting. When impairment creates patient risk — as in prescribing a teratogenic drug without checking pregnancy status — immediate action is required under the NMC Act 2020.

overallFeedback.feedback: The NMC Act 2020 is clear: impairment that creates patient risk must be reported regardless of the colleague's seniority. Eight to twelve percent of physicians experience substance use disorders over a career. The most dangerous impaired colleague is one functional enough that peers rationalise inaction.
Exactly. The NMC Act 2020 is unambiguous: impairment that creates patient risk must be reported. Seniority, collegiality, and discomfort do not override patient safety.
